build: Sprint 9 — the two admin surfaces: Documentation editor & Console Monitor
note: Scoped 2026-08-08 from the two disabled 'soon' rows in Sidebar.tsx:49-50, the only unfinished entries in the app shell. Verified against the tree: neither has a route. Documentation was never possible because the six public /docs pages are 929 lines of hand-authored JSX in content/docs.tsx, so the CMS is a storage-format change first and a UI second. Console Monitor is the reverse: the authenticated monitors room, target-app registry, capped console-logs relay and /api/console-logs/targets all exist in server.ts, and hooks/useBugTrackerSocket.ts already consumes every event — but the hook has ZERO call sites, an orphan from the 2026-07-24 UI reset. It is also missing an authorization level: the monitors room admits any signed-in user, not just admins. Sprint 8 (real-time issue stream) was scoped and never started; archived intact under .agents/docs/archive/sprint-8-realtime-issue-stream-* and re-scopeable as written.

features.title: DocPage model, migration, and the six pages converted to Markdown
features.description: S9-D1 + S9-D2. JSX cannot round-trip through a textarea, so the storage format has to change before any editor can exist. Body is one Markdown string with container directives; the TOC is derived from headings at read time rather than stored, so there is one editable structure instead of two.
steps: DocPage: slug @unique, title, group, groupOrder, order, summary, body, status draft|published, updatedAt, updatedById
Migration applied — stop the :3000 dev server first, prisma generate EPERMs on Windows otherwise
A one-time script converts all six pages in content/docs.tsx to Markdown + directives
The conversion diff is reviewed page by page; the SDK page is expected to need hand-finishing
content/docs.tsx STAYS in the tree until F010 passes — the JSX is otherwise only in git
features.notes: 2026-08-09. DocPage model + `prisma db push` (no migrations dir in this repo — db push is the convention). The six bodies were converted BY HAND into src/scripts/docs-content/*.md and seeded by scripts/seed-docs.ts (npm run seed:docs), idempotent by slug and refusing to clobber an admin edit without --force. Conversion reviewed page by page against the JSX block sequence: section counts 3/4/6/6/4/4 and every table shape (3c5r, 2c5r, 2c3r, 3c9r, 2c4r+2c6r, 2c7r, 2c5r) match the originals. content/docs.tsx stayed in the tree until F010, as the spec required.

features.title: Markdown + directive renderer over the existing DocsPrimitives
features.description: S9-D1. Plain Markdown was rejected: Callout, Endpoint and Table carry most of what makes the SDK and Quickstart pages readable. Directives map onto the eleven primitives that already exist, so there is one rendering path rather than a second look-alike.
steps: :::callout{tone title}, :::endpoint{method path}, tables, fenced code with lang all render through DocsPrimitives
Rendered output for a migrated page matches the pre-migration screenshot
An unknown directive degrades to plain text rather than throwing — one bad edit must not blank a public page
FAILURE CASE: a malformed directive does not take down the whole page render
features.notes: 2026-08-09. lib/docsMarkdown.ts (pure parser) + components/docs/DocsMarkdown.tsx (renderer over the existing DocsPrimitives). No Markdown library: every mainstream one emits an HTML string, and the only way to mount one is dangerouslySetInnerHTML — see F003. Directives: :::callout{tone,title}, :::endpoint{method,path} and inline :endpoint[GET /path] for table cells, plus a {w-44} width suffix on header cells so migrated tables keep their proportions. 19 unit tests + 5 rendered-output tests. Unknown directive degrades to a paragraph and an unterminated callout leaves the following sections intact — both asserted.

features.title: The escaping allowlist — raw HTML never reaches the DOM
features.description: S9-D4. /docs is public and unauthenticated on purpose; the SDK snippet lives there. Piping admin-authored Markdown into dangerouslySetInnerHTML turns one compromised admin account into stored XSS on the most public page in the product.
steps: Raw HTML in source is escaped and rendered as text
href is restricted to http:, https:, mailto: and same-origin relative paths
javascript: hrefs are dropped, not rendered
FAILURE CASE: a body containing renders inert, asserted on rendered output in a test
features.notes: 2026-08-09. Escaping is STRUCTURAL, not a step: the parser produces a typed tree and the renderer emits React children, so there is no HTML-string path to forget. Asserted on renderToStaticMarkup output (real rendered markup, no jsdom): and

features.title: /docs reads from the database, published-only, still anonymous
features.description: S9-D3. The public route filters to published so an editor's in-progress keystrokes are not live. The route staying anonymous is not incidental — gating install instructions behind a login is how a one-line integration turns into a support conversation.
steps: All six pages render at /docs/* from the DB, signed out
A draft page does not appear in the sidebar and its slug redirects to the default page
The TOC lists the same headings the JSX version did and anchors clear the sticky header
FAILURE CASE: an unauthenticated request for a draft slug leaks neither body nor title
features.notes: 2026-08-09. GET /api/docs and /api/docs/:slug, no authenticate, status published in the WHERE clause rather than filtered after the read. Observed signed out in the browser: all six pages render from the DB, rail groups in the original order (Get started/SDK/Concepts/API reference), TOC ids match the h2 ids exactly, scroll-margin-top computes to 96px so anchors clear the 64px sticky header. Draft check: flipped grouping to draft — it left the list, /docs/grouping redirected to /docs/overview with neither title nor body in the DOM, and the API returned 404 (not 403, which would confirm it exists).

features.title: Admin docs CRUD API, authorize('admin') on every route
features.description: Hiding a sidebar link is presentation, not access control — Sidebar.tsx:26 says so about this exact group. Every route gates server-side, and it is asserted per route because a gate applied to four of five routes is the shape this codebase has already been bitten by.
steps: List, read, create, update, publish/unpublish, delete, reorder
Slug uniqueness is enforced at the DB and surfaced as a field error, not a 500
Slug edits are permitted behind a confirmation naming the broken-link consequence (S9-D8)
FAILURE CASE: a non-admin gets 403 on EVERY route, asserted per route, not on one representative
features.notes: 2026-08-09. /api/admin/docs — list, read, create, update (status included, so publish/unpublish is not a second way to write one column), reorder in a transaction, delete. authenticate + authorize(admin) on the ROUTER, not per route. Slug collision caught from the unique index as P2002 and returned as a 409 with field:slug, not pre-checked (two admins racing would lose that check). Criterion 9 asserted PER ROUTE on the wire: GET/ GET/:id POST PATCH POST/reorder DELETE all 403 for a signed-in non-admin, all 401 anonymous, 200 for the admin.

features.title: /admin/docs — editor, preview, reorder
features.description: S9-D3. Preview renders through the same renderer as the public page, which makes preview a guarantee rather than an approximation. Built on the AdminUsers page pattern so the admin surfaces read as one thing.
steps: Edit Quickstart's body, publish, reload /docs/quickstart — the change is there, no rebuild, no restart
Draft preview and the public page produce identical rendered output for the same body, asserted by diff not by eye
Reordering within a group changes the public sidebar order on reload
Route is admin-gated client-side AND server-side; the row is ready: true
features.notes: 2026-08-09. /admin/docs — rail with drafts badged, editor, preview, reorder, delete, slug-rename confirmation naming the broken-link consequence (S9-D8). Criterion 3: edited Quickstart in the editor, saved, reloaded /docs/quickstart — the new section was live with no rebuild and no restart, and the derived TOC picked up its heading. Criterion 5 PROVEN BY DIFF, not by eye: the preview pane and the public page produced byte-identical section HTML (7317 chars, first difference at index -1). Criterion 6: Move up on Quickstart reordered the public rail on reload (quickstart > overview > …), then seed --force restored it. Reorder renumbers the whole group rather than swapping two values, because the seeded rows share positions.

features.title: The monitors room gates on role === 'admin'
features.description: S9-D5. The room refuses anonymous sockets but admits any signed-in user, and it carries every target app's console output. Shipping an Administration-labelled route over that transport makes a hidden link the only protection. Deliberately landed BEFORE the page: gate-after means the insecure version is the one that exists longest and gets demoed.
steps: Role is read from the database at join time, the way authorize() does it, never from a JWT claim
A signed-in non-admin emitting register{clientType:'monitor'} is refused
FAILURE CASE: that non-admin receives ZERO console-logs frames, asserted on the wire, not by an empty UI
FAILURE CASE: the anonymous target-app path still registers and still relays — io.use is NOT tightened as a side effect
features.notes: 2026-08-08. Policy extracted to lib/monitorAccess.ts as a pure predicate because vitest.config.ts holds the server suite to pure functions — a rule inside an io.on('connection') closure cannot be covered at all. 8 unit tests. Wire steps 3 and 4 cannot be unit-tested, so src/scripts/verify-monitor-access.ts asserts them against a live server + DB: 5/5 PASS — admin admitted; non-admin refused with 'Insufficient permissions'; anonymous target-app still registered AND relayed; non-admin received ZERO console-logs frames; sentinel log not persisted. Reintroduced-bug proof run early (F010 step 1): reverting the role check to authenticated-only turned 4 tests red naming the privilege gap, reverted clean. Known gap appended as F012 rather than fixed silently.

features.title: /admin/console — target list and live stream
features.description: A port of the standalone page documented in archive/console-monitor.md into the app shell, driven by the orphaned useBugTrackerSocket hook. Empty state says the feed is live-only, so a blank panel is never read as 'no errors ever happened'.
steps: Every connected target app is listed; connect/disconnect updates within 2s without a reload
A console.error in a target app appears within 2s, once, with level, timestamp, source, app name and stack
Level filter, copy, clear and auto-scroll behave as the archived doc describes
The connection badge never reads connected over a dead feed; restart reconnects and the target list is correct
features.notes: 2026-08-08. Observed in the browser against a live server, DB and simulated target apps. Connect 0->1->2 with no reload; disconnect removed the chip in ~2ms (criterion 10). Logs arrived within 2s carrying level, timestamp, source, app name and stack; 'warn' normalised to WARNING (criterion 11). Level filter: All 13 -> Errors 3 (only ERROR rows) -> Warnings 4 (only WARNING) -> All 14; clear emptied both the list and the counter (criterion 12). Dead-feed proven with the API alive and the socket URL pointed at a closed port: badge read Offline, never Live, with the disconnect warning and 'Not connected to the feed' copy; pointing it back produced Live + the app list again (criterion 17). Non-admin at this URL saw the refusal panel, zero log rows and no leaked output. GAP FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: `source` was not rendered, which criterion 11 names explicitly - added as its own column and to formatLogLine. Replaced useBugTrackerSocket (zero call sites, orphaned by the 2026-07-24 UI reset) with useConsoleMonitor.

features.title: Pause buffers, the ring buffer holds 500, nothing is persisted
features.description: S9-D6 + S9-D7. A pause that unsubscribes drops exactly the burst you paused to read. And server.ts:249-255 is explicit that persistence has one supported path — POST /api/ingest, keyed and rate limited. This sprint does not reopen that.
steps: Pause, generate 20 logs, resume — all 20 are there; a pending count showed while paused
The buffer holds at most 500 entries and drops oldest first
The panel does not degrade after 5 000 logs in a session
FAILURE CASE: after a session with hundreds of logs, SELECT count(*) FROM logs is unchanged
features.notes: 2026-08-08. Buffer rules live in lib/consoleBuffer.ts as pure functions - 16 unit tests - because a dropped burst and a bounded buffer are both invisible on screen and neither can be verified by looking at the page. Observed in the browser: paused with 9 visible, pending climbed 7->13->29 while the visible list stayed frozen at 9, and resume produced exactly 38 = 9 + 29, nothing dropped (criterion 13). Burst of 5000 logs from a second app left the buffer at exactly 500 with 500 DOM rows and a 0.1ms layout read, so the panel did not degrade (criterion 14). After ~5200 relayed logs the logs table held 22 rows, 0 of them from the monitor feed (criterion 18, S9-D6).

features.title: The suite proves its worth, and the JSX is deleted
features.description: A test that has never failed has proven nothing. The two failures this sprint is shaped to prevent are the privilege gap on the monitors room and stored XSS on a public page, so those are the two that get reintroduced. content/docs.tsx is deleted only here — once the DB path is proven, not before and not 'later'.
steps: Revert the monitors admit check to authenticated-only: the suite goes red naming the privilege gap
Revert the HTML escaping: the XSS test goes red
Both revert clean and the suite goes green
content/docs.tsx deleted in the same commit that flips /docs to the DB path
features.notes: 2026-08-09. Both reintroduced-bug proofs run, both reverted clean. (1) monitors admit reverted to authenticated-only: 4 server tests red naming the privilege gap. (2) The two docs defences reverted — paragraphs through dangerouslySetInnerHTML and the href allowlist removed: 8 client tests red, including all four rendered-output XSS assertions. Restored: server 61/61, client 44/44. content/docs.tsx deleted in the same commit that flips /docs to the DB path, as the spec required — and the JSX was rendered from git one last time first, to diff it against the migration (see progress.md).

features.title: Clean build, green suite, sidebar rows live, docs written
features.description: npm run build catches client errors tsc --noEmit misses here — the erasableSyntaxOnly gap. Both rows flip to ready: true only when the routes behind them refuse a non-admin server-side, not merely hide.
steps: tsc --noEmit, eslint src and npm run build clean in BOTH workspaces
npm test green in CI from a clean checkout
Both Sidebar.tsx rows are ready: true; a non-admin sees neither the rows nor a working route
admin-docs-and-console.md gains its exit notes; sprint-plan.md updated with what actually shipped
features.notes: 2026-08-09. tsc, eslint src, npm run build and vitest all clean in BOTH workspaces (server 61, client 44). One eslint suppression added with its reason: no-control-regex on the deliberate control-character strip in sanitizeHref. features.title: A demoted admin keeps monitoring until the socket reconnects
features.description: Found while implementing F007, appended rather than fixed silently. authorize() re-reads the role on EVERY request, so an HTTP demotion lands on the next call. A socket joins the monitors room once and stays, so the equivalent demotion does not land until that socket drops — a long-lived tab keeps streaming every target app's console output after the admin bit is removed. Not a regression: the room previously admitted any signed-in user, so this is strictly narrower than what shipped before. It is the residual window, not a new hole.
steps: Decide the mechanism: periodic re-check sweep over connectedClients.monitors vs. re-check before fan-out vs. accept-and-document
Demote an admin with a live monitor socket; the socket stops receiving console-logs within the chosen window
The evicted socket is removed from connectedClients.monitors, not merely muted
FAILURE CASE: the sweep does not add a database read per relayed log batch — that path is hot
features.notes: Deliberately NOT built inside F007: F007's steps do not ask for it, and widening a feature mid-loop is how a ledger stops matching what was verified. Sized as medium because the window closes on any reconnect, deploy or token refresh.
